label: choose a greeting that fits the time of day
note: Chapter 68. The old note was right on both counts -- the track omitted all four greeting concepts AND the four time words -- and chapters 66 to 68 fixed both halves: SPINE-TIME-OF-DAY now realizes 8 of its 9 concepts and omits only GREETING-DAY, which is exactly the shape the six tracks that already realize this node converge on. The chapter costs ONE new word: shubh, in front of parts of the day chapter 66 already taught. It also refuses two things on the page. The night is left out, because its greeting builds on raatree rather than the bare raatra and would be mis-built by the pattern; and the three greetings are taught for READING, since namaskaar -- the first word of the track, and already a culture claim as Marathi's default all-purpose greeting -- is what is actually spoken at any hour. Same treatment Hindi's suprabhaat lesson gives the same problem.
